classification_reason: Every CLI read surface (search, search --content, inspect, note-read, bootstrap --brief) reflected the hand edit immediately under a new snapshot id. A write guarded by the stale published snapshot failed closed with STALE_SNAPSHOT and named the actual snapshot. The published manifest and Markdown views stayed stale; only `validate` warned (HYGIENE-VIEWS). The views' own 'Generated:' stamp cannot reveal the staleness, contrary to the README's human-fallback advice.

consumer.goal: Build views, hand-edit one canonical note body, and check each read surface for staleness without regenerating
commands: baseline: los search memtable; los search zqxmemtab; los search 'definitely not here' --type note --content; los search zqxabsent --type note --content; los inspect note-lsm-trees; los note-read note-lsm-trees; los related note-lsm-trees; los bootstrap --brief; validate --compact --no-report; los status
sed: memtable→zqxmemtab, 'definitely not here'→'zqxabsent' in the note body
same surface set after the edit
los capability capture.create with expected_snapshot from generated/manifest.json
confusions: bootstrap --brief exposes the new snapshot id but says nothing about the published manifest lagging behind it
consumer.outcome: The CLI always answered from the current files. A human reading generated/*.md, or an interface reading generated/manifest.json, saw the old text with no in-file sign of staleness. `make views` fixed it.

internal.transaction_behavior: capture.create with the published (stale) snapshot → STALE_SNAPSHOT, retryable true, details {expected 82bc…, actual 9543…}; nothing written
internal.approval_behavior: approval subject computed with intent_sha256; refusal came from the snapshot guard
internal.projection_activity: CLI reads project in memory from canonical files and do not republish generated/; `make views` republished
internal.derived_changes: after make views: generated/backlinks.json and generated/manifest.json changed; manifest snapshot 82bc…→9543…, summary updated; Markdown views byte-identical (the body is not shown in them)
warnings_errors: W HYGIENE-VIEWS: generated/manifest.json is not the current authored snapshot — run `make views` (validate only)

friction.description: only way to see whether the published manifest lags was to open generated/manifest.json and compare _generated.snapshot_id with bootstrap's snapshot_id
README advises judging staleness by the Generated: timestamp, which is the last-commit time

surfaces.los search (summary): fresh — old term 'memtable' no longer found, new term found
surfaces.los search --type note --content: fresh — new snapshot 9543…, exact line snippet of the new text; old phrase 0 hits
surfaces.los inspect note-lsm-trees: fresh — summary shows the edited first paragraph (single inspect carries no snapshot id)
surfaces.los related note-lsm-trees: fresh (unaffected: lists concept + source only; body edit changes nothing there)
surfaces.los bootstrap --brief: fresh — new snapshot_id 9543…; no mention that generated/ lags
surfaces.los status: stale-silent for views — 'validation: OK · 3 warning(s)', views not named
surfaces.generated/manifest.json: stale-silent — old summary, old snapshot_id, same Generated stamp
surfaces.generated/*.md views: stale-silent — body text not shown in views; stamp unchanged and cannot change

scenario_record.write_against_stale_published_snapshot: STALE_SNAPSHOT (fail closed, actual snapshot in details)

uncertainties: Whether the Obsidian UI reads generated/manifest.json directly (and so shows stale text) is NOT TESTED
